blocks.text: The relationship between יהוה and
Yahushua

blocks.html: The relationship between יהוה and Yahushua is not difficult to understand. It is that of Father and Son. The same relationship we have with our Father in Heaven. יהוה is not only the Father of Yahushua but He is the Father of all His sons in the same way. In the physical shadow of earthly father and son; and the spiritual parallel that shadow represents… the father and son are not the same “being”. One begets the other. One is an “image” of the other. יהוה has always revealed Himself as our Father as Yahushua too confirmed. We see that יהוה is Yahushua’s Elohim and Father as Yahushua is no different that you and I:

blocks.html: All the references to Father and son in Scripture are in context of the Hebraic mindset of the place and authority of the father over his household. It is within this context that Yahushua as the son and “perfect image” of the Father is understood. Yahushua is the proxy of His Father יהוה as His instrument and assistant as Yahushua is seated at his Father יהוה’s right hand. The Universe is still the property of The Creator; the responsibility to govern it is given over to His sons.

blocks.html: 2. PLACE AND AUTHORITY. The position and authority of the father as the head of the family is expressly assumed and sanctioned in Scripture as a likeness of that of the Almighty over his creatures. It lies, of course, at the root of that so-called patriarchal government (Gen. 3:16; I Cor. 11:3)... While the father lived, he continued to represent the whole family, the property was held in his name, and all was under his superintendence and control... The children, and even the grandchildren, continued under the roof of the father … The property of the soil, the power of judgment, the civil rights belonged to him only, and his sons were merely his instruments and assistants...

10 Attributes of Yahushua’ relationship with his Father
1) Yahushua is a reflection of his Father

blocks.html: Yahushua works as his Father works. Yahushua imitates his Father, he does what he sees his Father do. Yahushua said, “My Father is working until now, and I am working.” And he also said, “The Son can do… only what he sees the Father doing.” (Yochanan/Yochanan 5:17,19)

2) Yahushua is dependent on his Father

blocks.html: He “can do nothing of his own accord.” (Yochanan 5:19)
blocks.text: He “can do nothing of his own accord.” (Yochanan 5:19)
3) Yahushua has faith in His Father’s love for him

blocks.html: “For the Father loves the Son,” Yahushua says. (Yochanan 5:20) This is where Yahushua’ security comes from. He doesn’t put his faith in human beings’ love for him. In fact, where his own self worth is concerned, he doesn’t care about anyone’s opinion, other than his Father’s. Yahushua didn’t “entrust himself” to people. (Yochanan 2:24) His security came from his faith in His Father’s love for him.

4) The Father allows Yahushua to see himself at work

blocks.html: The Father “shows him all that He Himself is doing.” (Yochanan 5:20)
blocks.text: The Father “shows him all that He Himself is doing.” (Yochanan 5:20)
5) Yahushua trusts and has confidence in his Father

blocks.html: “And greater works than these will he show him, so that you may marvel.” (Yochanan 5:20) Yahushua was sure, he knew, he trusted that the works his Father told him were to come, would come. His raising Lazarus from the dead. His own resurrection. And the pouring out of the Ruach Ha Qodesh. These were all yet to come but Yahushua trusted and had confidence in his Father, that He would come through.

blocks.html: 6) Yahushua and his Father work together in the same business, the business of giving life, of bringing the dead to life

blocks.html: “For as the Father raises the dead and gives life, so also the Son gives life to whom he will.” (Yochanan 5:21 and Yochanan 5:24-29)

7) The Father gives great responsibility to Yahushua

blocks.html: The Son of Man, who is יהוה’s Son, has lived life inside human skin. He’s walked where we walk, experienced what we experience, and suffered beyond what we suffer. He’s been misunderstood and mistreated in a way no one else has in all of human history. This makes him perfectly qualified to judge, so the Father “has given him authority to execute judgment, because he is the Son of Man.” (Yochanan 5:22, 27)

8) There’s no competitive spirit between Yahushua and his Father

blocks.html: There is perfect harmony. Yahushua says, he, Yahushua, is to be honoured “just as they honour the Father who sent him.” (Yochanan 5:23)

blocks.html: “…I seek not my own will but the will of Him who sent me.” (Yochanan 5:30)

10) Yahushua’ validation comes from his Father

blocks.html: Yochanan the Baptist bore witness to Yahushua but Yahushua says that the testimony Yahushua cares about isn’t from man. The testimony that matters to Yahushua is יהוה’s testimony. And יהוה spoke audibly, affirming and validating his Son in Matt. 3:13-17, Matt. 17:1-8, and Yochanan 12:27-30. יהוה spoke these words in the first, middle, and last parts of Yahushua’ public ministry, in the first, second, and third year. (Yochanan 5:31-37)
